top_choice_rationale: P002 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) rests on a specific physical idea, the magic-wavelength cancellation of light shifts for a trapped many-atom ensemble, which was reproduced in Sr, Yb and Hg laboratories with agreeing uncertainties near 1e-18 and compared over fibre links; the two-name allocation covers concept and performance cleanly. I weigh the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and the unchecked priority dates as real costs, and I rank P001 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) a close second: a new, well-confirmed phase with a clear experiment, though with a visible credit gap (BHZ, 3D work). Both are clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no collaboration with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp, only general membership of the atomic physics community
